metaTitle: Restoration Marketing for Water, Fire and Mold Work
metaDescription: Restoration marketing from ASP: local SEO, water damage Local Services Ads, storm-timed content and call tracking tied to booked jobs, all in your name.
intro: Restoration marketing has to reach a property owner while the damage is fresh and they are choosing who to call. ASP runs local search, water damage Local Services Ads, storm-timed content and call tracking for restoration companies, and measures all of it against booked jobs.

sections.heading: How restoration demand works
paragraphs: Restoration work starts with damage, and water damage can't wait. EPA advises drying water-damaged areas and items within 24 to 48 hours to prevent mold growth. That window gives a homeowner little time to shop around, so being easy to find and quick to answer carries a lot of weight.

Some demand follows the calendar. In markets touched by the Atlantic hurricane season, the official season runs June 1 to November 30, with most activity between mid-August and mid-October. On the fire side, the US Fire Administration estimates 343,000 residential building fires in 2024, though not every fire leads to restoration work.

EPA guidance sends bigger mold and contaminated-water jobs to professionals. EPA says that in most cases a homeowner can handle a moldy patch under about 10 square feet themselves, but points larger water damage or mold beyond that to its professional remediation guide. It also advises calling a professional when the damage came from sewage or other contaminated water.

sections.heading: SEO and local search for restoration companies
paragraphs: Your Google Business Profile has to match how you operate. Google allows a service-area business one profile, or one per location when each location has its own service area and staff, and says the service area should not extend farther than about two hours of driving from where you are based, though larger areas can suit some businesses.

On the website, water damage, mold remediation, and fire and smoke damage each need their own page. IICRC publishes a separate ANSI standard for each one (S500, S520 and S700), and EPA tells homeowners hiring a mold contractor to check experience and references and to ask that the work follow EPA, ACGIH, IICRC or other professional or government guidelines. A page that names the standards you follow answers that question before the call.

Some content earns trust by being straight with people. FEMA's flood insurance program states that most homeowners insurance does not cover flood damage, and a page that explains this plainly, without promising what any policy will pay, helps a homeowner understand their situation. StormFront, our weather-triggered content system, publishes timed posts when water or storm damage events hit your service area. We don't buy links, and organic work is reported against booked jobs.

sections.heading: Local Services Ads, Google Ads and Meta for restoration
paragraphs: Google's US Local Services Ads list includes a water damage services category, described as cleaning and inspecting water damage issues such as mold, sewage and paint damage. Screening for that category requires IICRC certification, on top of background checks for select users, general and professional liability insurance, and state-level licenses where local law applies. Once you are running, LSA rank weighs your bid along with review volume and response time, so we manage it against those signals.

As of October 15, 2026, the US list has no separate category for fire and smoke damage or for mold-only work, and Google notes that in some states, professionals may need additional licenses for mold remediation or assessment. Google Search Ads cover that ground, with one ad group per service so you can see which line is paying.

Meta plays a different role. Emergency work gets searched for at the moment it happens, so we use Facebook and Instagram to make your name familiar in the service area beforehand and to bring back people who visited your site, not to chase emergency calls.

sections.heading: How restoration results are measured
paragraphs: Each lead gets traced from the first call to the booked job and the revenue it produced. Call tracking assigns a number to each source, forms capture campaign tags, and lead source is carried into your CRM wherever that CRM supports it.

If you run Housecall Pro, ASP is an Official Housecall Pro Affiliate Partner and can send completed-job revenue back to Google Ads as offline conversions. In every account, the conversion action stays set to a real lead, so reports count real leads, not page views.

sections.heading: What you own
paragraphs: Everything ASP builds for a restoration company is registered to the company: the domain and site code, the Business Profile and its reviews, the Google, Local Services Ads and Meta ad accounts, and the CRM data. You pay the ad platforms yourself, so ASP never holds or marks up your spend.
When an engagement ends, those assets transfer with no handover or exit fee. The full breakdown is on our What You Own page.

faqs.question: What does a restoration marketing agency do?
faqs.answer: It gets a water, fire or mold restoration company found when damage happens and proves which channels produced booked jobs. ASP runs local search, service pages, Local Services Ads, Google Search Ads, Meta and StormFront content, with call tracking tied to your CRM.

faqs.question: Do I need IICRC certification to run Local Services Ads?
faqs.answer: For Google's water damage services category in the US, yes. Google's screening lists IICRC certification along with background checks for select users, liability insurance and state licenses where they apply. Google sets these requirements and can change them.

faqs.question: Can I advertise fire and mold restoration on Local Services Ads?
faqs.answer: Google's US category list had no separate fire and smoke or mold-only category as of October 15, 2026. The water damage category's description does mention mold. For fire and mold work beyond that, we use Google Search Ads with their own ad groups.

faqs.question: How does StormFront work for restoration companies?
faqs.answer: StormFront watches your service area and publishes targeted content when qualifying weather events hit, including water and storm damage events. It is $549 a month on its own and is included in our Foundation tier.

faqs.question: How much does restoration marketing cost?
faqs.answer: Foundation is $2,500 a month, and Growth, which adds paid media management, is $3,850 a month. Ad spend is separate and paid to the platforms. See the pricing page for the full breakdown.

faqs.question: Who owns my Business Profile and ad accounts?
faqs.answer: You do. You stay the primary owner of your Business Profile, and ASP works inside it as a manager you can remove. Your ad accounts are in your name too, as our What You Own page explains.
